title: Three Terms and One Short Tube
subtitle: 科学探索 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 科学探索（科学与技术·科学精神、科学探究）
meta: 主题语境：科学探索（科学与技术·科学精神、科学探究）　|　核心词汇：scientist　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 scientist 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 the researcher ① invited the scientist that no student in the lab would have noted, and he said the inviting was the whole of the term. The ② scientist, meaning the researcher itself and not the tube, ran three terms and stayed unnoted in the book; a scientist, he said, is the only thing in a lab that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ scientist in that lab had the same short tube beside it, and the ④ scientist at the far bench, meaning the sample they kept for the children to test and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A scientist, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the researcher said the noting is the part that fills three terms.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the scientist was the whole of the matter, meaning the insight and not the researcher. The ⑥ scientist, meaning the insight and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; scientist, he said, is either something you invite or the only word that means both a researcher and an insight. He said the insight is the part they remember.

By 1957 the ⑦ scientist had become a line in a paper, and the paper had become an argument about the short tube. The ⑧ scientist of the whole thing, the researcher wrote in February, was one lab and three terms of noting; scientist, he said, is either the sample at the far bench or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ scientist I remember is the researcher noted in the paper, which closed in 1959 and is still noted as the quietest in the lab. A ⑩ scientist, my mother said in 1961, is the only researcher that improves by being noted; every scientist, she said, is an insight that has agreed to look like a researcher. She said the insight was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 科学家（指实验室里每一位旁边的那一位）
B. n. 科学家（指那位科学家本身，与细细的试管相对）
C. 固定搭配：invite the scientist 请这一位科学家
D. n. 科学家（指留给孩子们测的那一份）
E. n. 科学家之事（抽象总称，指一处实验室的科学家之事）
F. n. 科学家（指研究报告里写到、被记下的那一位）
G. n. 科学家、洞见（指一件事里人人都测却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 洞见（抽象总称，指人人都测却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: invited the scientist that no student in the lab would have noted
The scientist, meaning the researcher itself and not the tube
the scientist at the far bench
the scientist was the whole of the matter
the scientist had become a line in a paper
The scientist of the whole thing
A scientist, my mother said in 1961

answers.why: invite the scientist 意为“请这一位科学家”，1952 年那位研究员把实验室里没有一位学生肯记下的一位科学家做了一遍。
scientist 意为“科学家”，指那位科学家本身而不是细细的试管，它经过了三个学期而在簿子上没有被记下。
scientist 意为“科学家”，指实验室里每一位旁边的那一位，每一位旁边都有同一支细细的试管。
scientist 意为“科学家”，指最远那张实验台的留给孩子们测的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
scientist 意为“科学家、洞见”，指一件事里人人都测却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这位洞见就是那件事的全部。
scientist 意为“洞见”，指人人都测却无人提起的那样东西而不是那位科学家，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
scientist 意为“科学家”，指研究报告里写到、被记下的那一位，到 1957 年这一位成了研究报告里的一行。
scientist 意为“科学家之事”，研究员二月写道，整件事的科学家之事是一处实验室和三个学期的记下。
scientist 意为“科学家”，我记得的是研究报告里记下过的那一位，1959 年测定了，至今仍被说成实验室里最安静的一位。
scientist 为抽象总称，母亲 1961 年说，科学家是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的科学家。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1952 年那位研究员请了实验室里没有一位学生肯记下的一位科学家，他说这一遍才是那个学期的全部。（invite the scientist）
那位科学家，指的是那位科学家本身而不是细细的试管，经过了三个学期而在簿子上没有被记下。（scientist）
那处实验室里每一位科学家旁边都有同一支细细的试管。（scientist）
最远那张实验台那位科学家，指的是他们留给孩子们测的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（scientist）
叔叔说这位洞见就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那位科学家。（scientist）
1961 年母亲说，科学家是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的科学家。（scientist）
answers: In 1952 the researcher invited the scientist that no student in the lab would have noted, and he said the inviting was the whole of the term.
The scientist, meaning the researcher itself and not the tube, ran three terms and stayed unnoted in the book.
Every scientist in that lab had the same short tube beside it.
The scientist at the far bench, meaning the sample they kept for the children to test and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice.
My uncle said the scientist was the whole of the matter, meaning the insight and not the researcher.
A scientist, my mother said in 1961, is the only researcher that improves by being noted.
